title: Unsubstantiated finite-search claim ((S) vs (N)) + missing verification note

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
NON-LOAD-BEARING but should be fixed. Remark "Why both (S) and (N)" item (ii) (solution.tex:113-124) asserts the existence of a strictly monotone functional F on M_{o→o} that violates non-strict monotonicity (N), "verified by a finite search; see the verification note" — but no such note is included. The closing paragraph (solution.tex:576-578) likewise says the strict-drop/strict-decrease inequalities "were checked numerically … with no violation."

These numeric appeals are not part of the formal proof (the inequalities are also proved symbolically), and the existence claim only MOTIVATES baking (N) into membership; the theorem does not depend on it. As written, the document presents an unproved combinatorial fact as established and references a missing artifact.

FIX (either): (a) exhibit an explicit witness F on a finite sub-poset of M_{o→o} (a small table: a≤a′ not <-everywhere, with F(a)>F(a′), while F is strict for the everywhere-< order), inline; or (b) demote to: "we do not rely on whether (S) implies (N); we simply impose (N), which is preserved by all operations," deleting the unsupported existence claim and the dangling "verification note" reference.

Note: even if (S)⟹(N) were TRUE, imposing (N) is harmless and the main proof is unaffected — this gap does not threaten correctness.
